<!-- FORGE:INVESTIGATOR -->
## Investigation Report

### Verdict / Confidence / Severity / Task Type
- Verdict: confirmed
- Confidence: high
- Severity: medium
- Task type: correctness and regression-test fix

### Root Cause
Workflow label derivation is split between canonical label constants and a partial hard-coded helper in the child runtime. Child checkpoint starts cover only some stages, and parent-owned merge transitions do not project the awaiting-merge and merged labels at their durable boundaries. The existing projector already safely replaces stale workflow labels and preserves unrelated labels.

### Evidence
- `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts` exports `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE` but no shared phase/action mapping.
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` maps investigate, build, and review starts plus investigation completion, but omits parent merge transitions and duplicates canonical label strings.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` queues and starts merge before gate evaluation, then merges and completes the phase without a corresponding workflow-label projection; the later terminal path uses a hard-coded merged label.
- `src/adapters/github-projection.ts` filters all existing `workflow:*` labels and appends the requested label through the existing PUT path, preserving unrelated labels.
- Current tests do not exercise every child lifecycle mapping, investigation classification branch, parent merge mapping, or repeated stale-label replacement.

### Affected Files
- `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts` — add one typed canonical checkpoint-to-label helper.
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts` — reuse the helper and prevent child checkpoints from claiming parent-owned merge/close/cleanup phases.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` — use the helper for awaiting-merge after gate approval and merged after successful merge checkpoint.
- `test/core/artifact-protocol.test.ts` — test all lifecycle mappings and investigation classification.
- `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts` — test repeated replacement while preserving unrelated labels.

### Recommendation
Centralize phase/action derivation beside `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE`, retain the existing invalid-versus-ready investigation classification, keep the current projector unchanged, and place parent merge label writes after the merge gate and after durable merge completion respectively. Reuse the helper for the terminal merged projection so no parent path maintains a duplicate mapping.

### Related Issues
- No separate duplicate implementation is active; prior cancelled runs are historical and do not own the current run.

### Decomposition Assessment
The change is coherent and bounded to workflow-label derivation, child/parent projection timing, and focused regression tests. No product, UX, protected-branch, or security-authority decision is required.

### Acceptance Spec
- Child investigation start projects workflow:investigating.
- Child plan, prepare-worktree, implement, and verify starts project workflow:building.
- Child review start projects workflow:in-review.
- Investigation completion projects workflow:ready-to-build or workflow:invalid using the existing classification.
- Parent merge projects workflow:awaiting-merge only after the merge gate approves, and workflow:merged only after the successful merge effect and merge checkpoint.
- Every projection uses the existing replacement primitive so one workflow:* label remains and unrelated labels survive.
- Child checkpoint input cannot claim parent-owned merge, close, or cleanup phases.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT -->
## Builder Contract

### Objective
Ensure every supported ForgeDock workflow transition projects the canonical current workflow:* label, removes stale workflow labels through the existing projector, and preserves unrelated labels.

### Allowed Paths
- `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts`
- `src/agents/child-runtime.ts`
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts`
- `test/core/artifact-protocol.test.ts`
- `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts`

### Forbidden Changes
- Do not change GitHub authentication, leases, state journal, review authorization, merge authorization, close authority, cleanup authority, or protected-branch policy.
- Do not rewrite `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel` semantics or add direct GitHub mutation paths.
- Do not project workflow:merged before a successful merge effect and durable merge completion checkpoint.
- Do not remove unrelated issue labels or alter non-workflow labels.
- Do not add credentials, production data, issue-body content, generated artifacts, or unapproved verification commands.

### Invariants
1. Canonical label values remain defined by `WORKFLOW_LABEL_BY_STAGE`.
2. One shared typed `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` helper is the source for child checkpoint and parent merge label derivation.
3. Investigation completion preserves the existing invalid-versus-ready classification.
4. Child starts map investigate to investigating, plan/prepare-worktree/implement/verify to building, and review to in-review.
5. Parent merge maps gate-approved merge start to awaiting-merge and successful merge completion to merged.
6. Child checkpoint input cannot claim parent-owned merge, close, or cleanup phases.
7. Every write uses `GitHubIssueProjector.setWorkflowLabel`, which removes stale workflow:* labels and preserves unrelated labels.
8. The named `check` command is the only local verification command executed.

### Deliverables
- Typed shared checkpoint-to-workflow-label helper beside canonical label constants.
- Child runtime wired to the helper with no duplicate mapping and no parent-phase checkpoint authority.
- Parent merge awaiting/merged projections at the correct durable boundaries.
- Regression tests for lifecycle mapping, investigation classification, replacement, and unrelated-label preservation.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### History
- Issue #92 is a confirmed regression in the frozen staging base; prior cancelled attempts are historical and do not authorize reuse of their branches or commits.
- The projector already implements safe workflow-label replacement, so the defect is derivation and timing.

### Callers and Data Flow
- The child `forge_checkpoint` handler persists the typed event, projects its phase report, derives a workflow label, and calls the existing projector.
- `ForgeWorkOnController.#finalize` owns merge/close/cleanup. It must project awaiting-merge only after gate approval and project merged only after `mergePullRequest` succeeds and merge completion is journaled.
- `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts` is imported by both child and parent code after centralization.
- Adapter tests use a deterministic transport with a bug label and workflow labels to assert safe replacement.

### CI Surface
- The trusted policy authorizes `forge_verify` with name `check`, invoking `npm run check` in the assigned worktree.
- GitHub CI and parent-owned merge/close remain outside this writer's authority.

### Prior Findings
- The current child mapping is partial, hard-coded, and duplicated outside the canonical label constants.
- Parent merge transitions have no label projection at gate-approved merge start or immediately after merge completion.
- Existing tests cover only one exact label assertion and one isolated replacement.

### Hazards
- Setting awaiting-merge before the review gate could falsely advertise merge readiness.
- Setting merged before the merge effect/checkpoint could misrepresent durable state.
- Allowing child merge checkpoints would let child logic claim a parent-owned terminal label.
- Rewriting the projector could drop the unrelated bug label or multiple labels.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

## Implementation Plan

1. Add an exported typed `workflowLabelForCheckpoint` helper in `src/core/artifact-protocol.ts`, using canonical constants for child starts, investigation completion, merge start, and merge completion. Check IDs: `canonical-mapping`, `invalid-classification`.
2. Replace the child-runtime local mapping with the shared helper, use canonical phase types, and constrain the checkpoint schema to child-owned phases. Check IDs: `child-reuse`, `child-authority`.
3. Import the helper in `src/workflows/work-on.ts`; after an approved merge gate project awaiting-merge before invoking the merge effect, then after the merge effect and `appendPhase(..., "merge", "complete", ...)` project merged. Reuse the helper for the final terminal projection. Check IDs: `merge-awaiting`, `merge-merged`, `merge-ordering`.
4. Extend `test/core/artifact-protocol.test.ts` for all child starts, both investigation outcomes, and parent merge actions. Extend `test/adapters/github-projection.test.ts` for repeated stale workflow replacement with bug-label preservation. Check IDs: `mapping-tests`, `replacement-preservation`.
5. Inspect the frozen-base diff, run the approved `check`, create the implementation commit, prepare the bound PR, and run the required fresh reviewer panel. Check IDs: `diagnostics`, `diff-identity`, `verification`, `review-gates`.

### Acceptance Mapping
- `canonical-mapping`, `invalid-classification` → shared canonical helper and retained investigation branch.
- `child-reuse`, `child-authority` → child checkpoint lifecycle uses one helper and cannot claim parent phases.
- `merge-awaiting`, `merge-merged`, `merge-ordering` → parent labels align with gate and durable merge ordering.
- `mapping-tests`, `replacement-preservation` → lifecycle and safe replacement regression coverage.
- `diagnostics`, `diff-identity`, `verification`, `review-gates` → final diff, named check, commit, PR, and review evidence.

### Out of Scope
- GitHub authentication, state/CAS, leases, review/merge policy, close, cleanup, or branch protection.
- Changes to issue/PR content or label API design.
- New verification commands, CI changes, or runtime sandbox policy.
- Historical label reconciliation outside current transition paths.
